nominees.name: Peter Zoller

nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation
motivation: Cirac and Zoller turned Feynman's idea of quantum simulation into concrete physics. They proposed controlled quantum logic with trapped atoms and, with Jaksch and collaborators, showed that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model. Bloch's landmark 2002 observation of the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator transition confirmed that proposal and launched a new experimental paradigm. His later work added single-site-resolved imaging, many-body localization and the controlled study of quantum dynamics far from equilibrium. Together their contributions made synthetic quantum matter into a precise laboratory for strongly correlated physics, from Hubbard-model magnetism to gauge theories. This platform is now used by many laboratories worldwide, and it laid the conceptual and technical basis for today's programmable quantum simulators and neutral-atom quantum processors. A deep theoretical insight grew into a transformative experimental field that links fundamental many-body physics with quantum information science.
